solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Large drink, with which darts player gets leg over?

definitions.meaning: a measure of spirits twice the standard size, ordered at a bar

definitions.text: with which darts player gets leg over?
definitions.meaning: in darts a leg (a single game) must be finished by hitting the narrow outer ring that scores twice the segment's value

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg over' looks like slang, but a leg is one game of darts, won only by finishing on the outer ring of the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a twice-sized measure of spirits and the scoring ring that ends a darts game.

clue.text: Shop really for Chinaman, perhaps

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a kind of food shop
very, as in 'very good', means really

explanation.surface: Someone asks a shopkeeper for a Chinese customer, as if ordering in.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chinaman is a cricket term: a left-arm wrist-spinner's ball, one type of bowling delivery; 'perhaps' flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket every ball bowled is a delivery, and the Chinaman is one particular kind of spin ball.

clue.text: Hidden, as is only one domino?

definitions.meaning: not seen or noticed by anyone
in a standard set the double-blank tile alone carries no dots at all

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word literally: without spots, like the double-blank domino.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnoticed things go unseen, and a tile bare of dots is literally without spots.

clue.text: Rubbish issue

definitions.meaning: offspring, a brood of young animals born together

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both scattered waste and a set of young born to one mother at once.

clue.text: Sending unsolicited mail two miles into the country, heading for Grimsby

indicators.note: the two mile abbreviations go into the middle of the country's name

parts.note: Spain is the country
M is the abbreviation for mile, so two of them make MM

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, here taken from Grimsby

explanation.surface: Someone posts junk mail across Spain while bound for a fishing town in England.
explanation.walkthrough: Grimsby is an English port town; only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk email sent in bulk to people who never asked for it is the classic modern nuisance of that name.

clue.text: Telegraph upset about, say, Irish tabloid feature

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the two short abbreviations
upset means knocked over, so the newspaper's name is jumbled

parts.note: EG (for example) is what 'say' stands for

explanation.surface: A broadsheet newspaper is scandalised by a feature in an Irish tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' gives PAGETHREL, which 'about' splits round EGIR. The British Sun long printed a topless model on its third page, hence the tabloid feature.
explanation.definitionFit: The topless model printed on an inside page was a notorious regular item in British tabloid newspapers.

clue.text: Wonder if a small measure of liquid fills the bog

indicators.note: one piece fills another when placed inside it

parts.note: mire is boggy, swampy ground
CL is the abbreviation for centilitre, a small liquid measure

explanation.surface: Someone muses on whether a splash of water could ever fill a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wonder' looks like a verb opening a question, but it is a noun, the definition; 'if' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marvellous that seems beyond natural explanation is a wonder in the same sense.

clue.text: Small area of sea where I catch about fifty

indicators.note: the word for catch goes round the Roman numeral for fifty

parts.note: set, as in setting a snare, is to catch
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fisherman names the small stretch of sea where he lands about fifty fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a fishing spot; the definition loosely means a tiny patch of land within the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny island is a small area of land set within the sea around it.

clue.text: Death between the covers of gory magazine

indicators.note: the word for death sits between the two cover letters
the covers of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: loss, as in bereavement, is a death

explanation.surface: A grisly death story sits between the covers of a horror magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy is a magazine printed on shiny paper, usually about fashion or celebrities.

clue.text: Scorer, with his partner, drunk?

definitions.meaning: a composer, one who writes musical scores
Cockney rhyming slang 'Brahms and ___' means drunk, rhyming with a vulgar word for intoxicated

explanation.walkthrough: In British rhyming slang 'Brahms and Liszt' means drunk; the partner is the other composer, Brahms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian pianist was a composer of scores, and half of the rhyming slang pair meaning tipsy.

clue.text: A little smoke coming from car finally logical, I gathered

indicators.note: the letters are gathered up and assembled in a fresh order
finally picks the last letter of car

explanation.surface: Someone gets out of a car smoking, and reasons logically about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' rearranges RLOGICALI, the final letter of 'car' with LOGICAL and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarillo is a small thin cigar, literally a little smoke.

clue.text: I reach partner struggling as survivor of king

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters writhing into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to reach a partner who is struggling, after the king has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII's sixth wife outlived him, the only one of his queens to do so while still married to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's last queen was still alive when he died, so she survived the monarch.

clue.text: Bloody television finally in colour!

indicators.note: the final letter goes in the colour word

parts.note: violet is a colour

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of television

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that the television is at last showing colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' looks like a swearword exclamation, but it is the definition: gory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bloody involves bloodshed and brutal force, the same as savage.

clue.text: Roman historian, one involved in diplomacy with America

indicators.note: the numeral is involved in, put inside, the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact is diplomacy, skill in handling people
I is the Roman numeral for one
US is America

explanation.surface: An ancient historian works as a diplomat on behalf of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus wrote the Annals and Histories, accounts of the early Roman emperors.

clue.text: Admire speed

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to regard highly and the pace at which something moves.

clue.text: Bold French leader unable to take in conversation?

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter, here of French

parts.note: with no ears, a person cannot hear what is said

explanation.surface: A bold French leader is unable to follow a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable to take in conversation' is a whimsical way of saying without ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A bold person is brave and unafraid, which is the meaning here.

clue.text: Sweet thing from European capital almost entirely raised in squalid district

indicators.note: the turned capital goes in the word for a squalid district

parts.note: a slum is a squalid run-down district

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so backwards
almost entirely means lose the final letter

parts.note: Prague is the capital of the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: A sweet comes from a European capital that has risen almost entirely from its slums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' drops the capital's last letter, and 'raised' (reading upwards in a down clue) turns the rest to UGARP before 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugarplum is a small round sweet, a candy of boiled sugar.

clue.text: Inclination a number refuse, about a hundred

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: the word for refuse goes about, around, the numeral

parts.note: to deny is to refuse
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A certain number refuse something about a hundred times, showing their inclination.
explanation.definitionFit: An inclination is a leaning towards something, as is a tendency.

clue.text: Meticulous Manx?

definitions.meaning: thorough, attending to every small point
a Manx cat is born without a tail

explanation.walkthrough: The Manx cat, from the Isle of Man, has no tail; read the answer as de-tailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful work covering every small point is thorough; a tailless cat is jokingly without a tail.

clue.text: Assailant's ultimate motive for crime

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is the last, here of Assailant's

parts.note: a reason is a motive

explanation.surface: Detectives seek the attacker's real motive for a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country is a grave crime under law.

clue.text: Monster so backward

indicators.note: backward means the word for so is read in reverse

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so

explanation.surface: A monster is described as rather slow-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, a monster.

clue.text: Two whole circuits in half, perhaps, appearing cleaner

indicators.note: the two circles are put in the rearranged letters
perhaps says the letters of half may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: O is a complete circle or circuit, so two of them make OO

explanation.surface: A race of two full laps in half the time makes someone look cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the fodder to LFAH, and 'in' opens it after the L; a loofah is a bath sponge, the cleaner that the surface hides.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is a dried fibrous gourd used as a bath sponge for scrubbing the skin.

clue.text: Plate up for cat, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: Someone serves up a plate for the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat is one example of an animal; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Shameless individual securing degree by guile, ultimately

indicators.note: the word for individual secures, holds, the other letters inside

parts.note: one is a single individual
BSc is a Bachelor of Science degree

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of guile

explanation.surface: A shameless person gets a degree through cunning in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene behaviour offends decency, which is what shameless conduct does.

clue.text: Brush, sort of a plant

indicators.note: to sort letters is to put them in a new order

explanation.surface: A brush is described as a kind of plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brush' also means scrubland, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody bush, a plant.

clue.text: Passed over ridge on circling

indicators.note: circling means the letters move round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone passes over a ridge while circling.
explanation.definitionFit: To be passed over is to be overlooked or disregarded.

clue.text: Prevent everyone going behind the trees

indicators.note: the word for everyone goes behind, after, the trees

parts.note: a forest is a mass of trees
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone is stopped from going into the woods behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act first so as to stop something happening.

clue.text: Setter offered half of capital, which is juicy

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: half of means the first half of the word is used

parts.note: London is the UK capital

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that half of the capital is juicy.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large fruit full of sweet juice.

clue.text: Goddess going round a block in dance

indicators.note: the goddess's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods
a ban blocks something

explanation.surface: A goddess dances round a block.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a slow Cuban dance in duple time, famous from Carmen.

clue.text: Times covers green item well!

indicators.note: the word for times covers, goes around, the fruit

parts.note: by means times, as in multiplication: six by four
a lime is a green fruit

explanation.surface: A newspaper covers a green item, and someone exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the British newspaper, but it is BY, as in three by four.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise; blimey is British slang.
